summary: This Docusaurus plugin automatically creates individual routes for each article series in your blog. Instead of using a single parameterized route that Docusaurus can't validate, it builds a dedicated route for each series at build time (like `/series/writing-better-bash-scripts`), pointing them all to the same React component that displays the articles in that series. This approach lets Docusaurus's link checker verify that series links actually exist, rather than having to ignore all broken links site-wide.

explanations.32: The `path` module provides utilities for working with file and directory paths across different operating systems.
explanations.33: `normalizeUrl` is a Docusaurus utility that standardizes URL formatting, handling things like trailing slashes and locale prefixes consistently.
explanations.34: This imports a helper function that scans your blog's article files and extracts all the unique series slugs mentioned in their front matter.
explanations.36: A Docusaurus plugin is a function that receives the build context and returns an object defining plugin behavior — things like what routes to create and which files to watch.
explanations.42: The `getPathsToWatch` method tells Docusaurus to monitor all blog article files, so when you add a new series to an article's front matter, the dev server automatically picks it up without restarting.
explanations.46: This loop runs once at build time, creating one route for each series that exists in your blog articles.
explanations.50: `normalizeUrl` combines the base URL, the literal string "series", and the series slug into a properly formatted route path, accounting for your site's locale and base configuration.
